scientific_summary: Selected early-ALS randomized16-week ALSFRS-R benefit at50mg IM twice weekly; earlier broader primary null; linked strength/respiratory nulls and component positives retained. Stronger controlled human functional design than niacin’s open-label observation, with no inferred MVA superiority.
integrated_planning_interpretation: Replace a broad impression that only 2020 plans are available with documented 2018 public specification of the core endpoint, population, dose and model, plus official UMIN2017 registration dates. Final detailed SAP timing, actual data lock/unblinding and exact history of all fields/analyses remain unverified.

sources.title: Patients' experiences with methylcobalamin injections in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
sources.design: Qualitative semi-structured interviews with patients and caregivers; two researchers coded four themes and eleven subthemes.
sources.findings: Subjective energy, fatigue and balance benefits reported alongside difficulty separating treatment effects from disease progression.
sources.role: Discovery context, not controlled efficacy confirmation
sources.exact_exposure: Not established from the saved abstract

intervention.formulation: Source-defined lyophilized injection; JETALS 25 mg mecobalamin per vial, two vials per 50 mg dose, total 4 mL administered at two intramuscular sites after saline reconstitution.
intervention.comparator: Placebo injection without mecobalamin; JETALS white lyophilized preparation.
intervention.supplier: Eisai provided JETALS active drug and placebo.
identity_locators: Earlier main Methods and current NCT00444613

design.masking: Double-blind trial with separate efficacy/ALSFRS assessors and injectors/safety assessors; red drug and urine precautions; no formal blinding-success validation obtained.
design.population: Adults at least 20 years, updated Awaji definite/probable/laboratory-supported ALS, onset within one year at observation entry, ambulatory outpatient severity grade 1 or 2, 1-2 ALSFRS-R point decline in 12-week observation, FVC >60%, no previous tracheostomy/noninvasive respiratory support.
design.background_care: Stable riluzole allowed; edaravone prohibited during blinded treatment and within four weeks before observation entry; rehabilitation and nutritional management allowed.

postrandomization_diagnostic_exclusions.reason: Alternative diagnosis of cervical spinal stenosis

design.denominator_limit: FAS excludes one randomized participant; outcome observations vary by visit. No blanket all-randomized ITT claim.

primary.endpoint: ALSFRS-R total change from randomization to week 16
primary.method: MMRM with baseline covariate, treatment, time, minimization factors and treatment-by-time interaction; no primary missing-value imputation.
primary.interpretation: Less deterioration in the selected population; both groups decline. Reported 43% is relative reduction of mean score decline, not percent recovery, strength improvement, survival benefit or response probability.

event_endpoint.endpoint: 24-hour noninvasive respiratory support, invasive respiratory support or death in main Table 2; protocol all-day NIV operationalized as at least 22 hours
event_endpoint.limit: No events over 16 weeks does not establish survival benefit; a placebo laryngotracheal separation for dysphagia and later stenosis are separately described.

components.hierarchy: Supplemental ALSFRS-R component analyses; no independent cohort
components.locator: Main Discussion; outcome supplement eTable 3, pp 7-8
components.limit: eTable 3 prints descriptive changes, not component P values. Raw total changes are not the adjusted primary estimates.

sensitivity.limit: Not every sensitivity specification is positive; planned PPS/AUC and missing-data alternatives are not all quantitatively reported.

subgroups.status: Multiple nominal supplemental contrasts; no demonstrated interaction or responder-selection rule

safety.source_window: Native Table 3 footnote includes observation and treatment
safety.unresolved: Main prose and eTable 5 reverse cerebral-infarction and hemorrhoid-operation arm attribution; severe/serious table labels also conflict. No silent reassignment.

design.population: Adults at least 20, ALS onset within 36 months, revised El Escorial/Airlie House categories, severity 1/2, 1-3 point ALSFRS-R decline during 12-week observation, FVC>60%, no ventilation/tracheostomy.
design.completion_limit: 95 full-period completions plus 165 event completions;260 is not full-duration exposure completion.

primary_overall.hierarchy: Two primary endpoints, four contrast tests, permutation multiplicity adjustment; overall primary efficacy not established.

event.definition: All-cause death or progression-related invasive/noninvasive ventilatory support for at least 22 hours

primary_overall.limit: Reported contrast statistics preserved as printed, not reanalysed or replaced with pairwise conventional P values.

missingness_and_changes.sample_plan: Blinded change from 300 patients/130 weeks to 360 planned/182 weeks following low event rates; two interim safety/futility reviews.
missingness_and_changes.analysis: Specified terminal/post-event observations, LOCF, withdrawal censoring and 28-day rules; deaths/no post-event assessments assigned worst ranks, with-999 a ranking placeholder rather than a clinical score.
missingness_and_changes.grip_handling: Values >0 and <5 kg treated as 0 in supplied SAP.
missingness_and_changes.endpoint_count_limit: Endpoint n is not a count of directly measured 182-week completers.

early_posthoc.definition: Diagnosed within 12 months after symptom onset
early_posthoc.status: Post hoc despite favorable signal; extensive onset-cutoff and prognostic-stratum explorations do not change overall primary null.
early_posthoc.locator: Main Table 2B; native Figure 2C-D; supplement Tables e-2,e-3,e-6

longterm.secondary_interpretation: Tables e-1/e-4 contain favorable and nonpositive exploratory contrasts. Overall combined-dose MMT/left grip/Norris P=.03 are retained, not called confirmatory significance: supplied SAP uses one-sided .025 for efficacy, and secondary multiplicity is uncontrolled.
longterm.additional_explorations: Tables e-2/e-3 scan onset cutoffs 7-24 months; e-5 selects prognostic factors in placebo using backward elimination; e-6/e-7 report onset, sex and FVC strata plus ALSFRS-R/Norris component results. Native e-7 early subgroup P values 50 mg/combined: ALSFRS bulbar .003/.007, motor .038/.044, respiratory .004/.020; Norris limb .038/.052, bulbar .002/.002. These are not additional independent studies or verified treatment interactions.

safety.limit: Progression manifestations generally excluded from adverse-event coding except death; no cross-population safety equivalence.

JETALS_design_subset_from_earlier.selection: Within one year at observation entry and 1-2 point run-in decline; different from 144-person early-diagnosis event subgroup.
JETALS_design_subset_from_earlier.limit: Target profile chosen after comparing earlier 1-2 versus 1-3 point decliners; comparison data not shown. Hypothesis generation, not independent confirmation.

trial_relationship.independence_limit: Distinct randomized cohorts but overlapping investigators/supplier and shared development program.

comparative_interpretation.functional_evidence: Randomized short-duration selected-population clinical-function benefit, with earlier overall null and exploratory favorable signal; not merely a biomarker or qualitative report.
comparative_interpretation.exposure_boundary: High-dose intramuscular source preparation, not ordinary oral B12 or cyanocobalamin.
comparative_interpretation.durability_boundary: JETALS controlled 16 weeks; earlier 182 week broad primary tests null; no controlled extension proof qualified.
comparative_interpretation.renewal_fidelity_boundary: No muscle/neuron renewal, chromosomal fidelity, BUB1B correction or BUBR1 restoration measurement.
comparative_interpretation.fair_competitiveness: Apply the same function/exposure/durability/renewal/fidelity standards used for compensation candidates. BUBR1 mediation is additionally required for restoration claims, not an extra exclusion condition for all functional comparisons.
